transcript: If you were a fan of last year's Tony winning revival of appropriate, but now you're sleeping on the new Broadway dramedy from the same playwright. I, I don't know, get it together. I think Brandon Jacob Jenkins is one of the most skilled playwrights working today, and purpose is his new play about the family of a famous black civil rights leader, all of whom have, in their own way, been damaged by public scandal or private conflict. To me, it was kind of about the messiness of being a flawed human being and a flawed family in the public eye, and how that exists in tension with this mythic ideal of greatness that society places on its heroes and leaders. There's a lot going on with this play. It's packed with drama that twists and turns and veers off into different tangents and ends up touching on a wide range of topics. And I know some people have criticized it for, like, trying to do too, too much, and I do get that. But honestly, there was hardly a single moment where I wasn't totally enthralled by it. Because this is a playwright who's just so skilled at writing engaging scenes and dialogue and compelling characters. And ultimately, even with all of the territory that the play covers, it all more or less comes back to the same few core ideas. If I had one real criticism, it's that I do think the second half is not quite As good as the first, first act is honestly super entertaining. It's a real delight to watch. I think it strikes just the right balance between being genuinely dramatic but also embracing an organic sense of humor and fun. Almost like watching a reality TV show if it were, like, super, super well written. In Act two, the quality of the writing, of the scenes, and the character development remained consistently strong, but it never quite built up to the climactic conclusion that it seemed like it was going for. I have to mention that the ensemble of actors here is pretty extraordinary. And no, not just my my fave Tony Award winner, Kara Young, really the entire cast. There is not a single weak link. And while I stand by all of my praise for the script itself, I also think that it's elevated by this rock solid production.
classificationReason: Creator shares a first-hand opinion on Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' 'Purpose', praising the writing, dialogue, and characters, and says they were 'totally enthralled' — clear personal review of this Broadway production.
